self-stimulation of the anterior part of basal forebrain (nucleus entopeduncular, nucleus commissure anterior, lateral hypothalamus, and preoptic area) in dogs is associated with a negative reaction to food, and that this negative reaction is manifested in three forms, namely ignoring food, food rejection, and food ejection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the effects of the self-stimulation of various sites of the anterior basal forebrain on the behavior of dogs.
the study of self-stimulation in 9 dogs in the anterior part (ventral and dorsal) of the basal fore brain.
the effects of self-stimulation on food intake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the dog the negative response to food during self stimulation is a phenomenon that occurs in the anterior part (anterior to the nucleus accumbens) of the basal fore brain, and is a function of the reward value of the stimulus.
the rewarding effect of the stimulus is due to the activation of a neural system controlling food intake.

in the anterior part, but not in the posterior part of the basal brain, self-stimulation of the rewarding sites can be accompanied by negativism to a food reward.
the rewarding value is determined by a balance between the excitatory and the inhibitory systems controlling the consummatory acts.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the food we eat is a major contributor to the development and maintenance of obesity.
the negative response to food is a reliable indicator of the rewarding value of a brain site.
the brain is capable of learning to like and dislike things, even when those things are not inherently good or bad for us.
